Chicago Ridge has 5,840 housing units and a median build year of 1973. 64 percent of them were built before 1980, 44.8 percent before 1970 and 1.1 percent before 1940. Those three numbers together describe the walls, the trim and the windows better than a photograph does.

Owner households here number 2,918 and renter households 2,391, a 55 percent owner-occupied place. The stock behind those households is 33.8 percent detached, 2.3 percent attached and 63.5 percent multi-unit, at a median of 4.8 rooms. The Census puts the median home value at $217,800.

Ranked against the 54 suburbs and towns covered here, Chicago Ridge lands in the top four on the most housing in buildings of two or more (63.5 percent) and the smallest homes by room count (4.8 rooms).

Set against the other places covered here, Chicago Ridge is furthest from the middle on three things: housing in buildings of two or more at 63.5 percent against a 29 percent average, prewar housing at 1.1 percent against a 15.8 percent average and townhomes and rowhouses at 2.3 percent against a 7.5 percent average.

Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, 2019-2023 (tables B25003, B25024, B25034, B25035, B25077). Every dollar figure on this page is a published Census estimate of what homes in the area are worth. None of it is a price for work.

How the age of the stock changes the work here

Interiors from around 1973 run to lower ceilings and more doors than a modern plan, and Chicago Ridge averages 4.8 rooms a unit. Six-panel doors, full baseboard runs and heavy casing: trim is where an interior job gets long. It is also the line most quotes leave vague, so ask for it on its own. 63.5 percent of the housing sits in buildings of two units or more, which means hallways, stairwells and unit turnarounds are as much of the work as living rooms. Those get quoted per unit and they get done to a date.

What should be on a written quote in Chicago Ridge

  • Setup does not shrink with the room. The median unit here is 4.8 rooms. Masking, cutting in and cleanup cost the same in a small room as a large one, so a flat per-room rate is usually wrong in one direction or the other.
  • Per unit, to a date. 63.5 percent of units here are in buildings of two or more. Turnover work is priced per unit and scheduled to a move-out, not to the weather.
  • Two different customers. 55 percent owner occupancy means homeowner work and landlord work sit side by side here, and they want opposite things from a schedule.
  • Distance, stated. Chicago Ridge is 2.9 straight-line miles from the shop. Travel to Chicago Ridge is not a hidden line item on this site and it should not be one on a written quote either.

What the housing here is likely made of

Most of it is 1970s stock with a large share of townhomes and apartment units. Association work, matching an existing scheme exactly and painting several identical units in a row, is as much of the Chicago Ridge market as single-house work.

It is read off exactly two things: the 1973 median build year, and the split between 33.8 percent detached houses, 2.3 percent attached homes and 63.5 percent in buildings of two units or more.

An inference, not a measurement. Neither the Census nor the regional housing data records what a wall in Chicago Ridge is made from, so no percentage is attached to it and none should be. Your own elevation settles it in four seconds from the sidewalk.

Lead-safe work on Chicago Ridge houses

The Census publishes a pre-1980 bucket rather than a pre-1978 one, and on that measure 64 percent of the housing sits on the older side of the line in Chicago Ridge. Anything built before 1978 sits inside the federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule the moment work disturbs its paint. Illinois never took the program on, so the agency behind it here is EPA itself.

Read it as a method rather than a prohibition. Below roughly six square feet of disturbed paint in a room, or twenty outside, it does not bite. Above that, and on any window replacement in Chicago Ridge at all, it decides how the room is sealed and how it is left. On 4.8-room housing that threshold arrives early.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Chicago Ridge.

Ask about it early. It changes the sequence of a job rather than the price of the paint, and a contractor who has thought about it will tell you in plain terms what happens on day one.

This site does not claim EPA lead-safe firm certification. No number has been supplied, so the trust panel below shows it as pending. Ask for it directly, from anyone quoting work in Chicago Ridge.

Questions

Asked about Chicago Ridge

Does the lead-safe rule apply to my house in Chicago Ridge?

Probably, and the honest answer is that your build year decides it rather than the town. 64 percent of housing units in Chicago Ridge went up before 1980, so most addresses here land on the pre-1978 side of the federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule. It applies to work that disturbs paint, at roughly six square feet per room inside or twenty square feet outside, and to any window replacement. Check the year on your own address and ask whoever quotes you how they handle it.

Do you paint rental units and common areas in Chicago Ridge?

Yes, and it is a real part of the work here rather than an afterthought. 63.5 percent of housing units in Chicago Ridge sit in buildings of two or more, and 2,391 households rent. Turnover repaints get priced per unit and scheduled around a move-out date. Ask for it that way and you will get a number that fits the deadline.

Is a smaller place cheaper to paint per room?

Not proportionally, no. The median unit in Chicago Ridge is 4.8 rooms, and a small room still needs the same masking, the same cutting in and the same cleanup as a large one. What falls is the roller time, which is the cheapest part of the day. Anyone quoting a flat per-room rate on small rooms is either guessing high or about to be disappointed.

How quickly can somebody look at it?

Chicago Ridge is 2.9 straight-line miles from the shop, which is close enough that looking at the work and doing the work do not have to be the same trip. That matters most on small jobs, because a repair that is worth doing gets seen instead of being pushed into a bigger job later. Call 708-935-4289.
